tagline: Five miles out of Orange to a mill village.
intro: Rapidan Road leaves Orange, which was Orange Court House until the late nineteenth century, and runs about five miles northeast to Rapidan, a village on both banks of the Rapidan River. It grew up in the late eighteenth century around the mill at Waugh's Ford, and milling lasted there into the mid-twentieth century.
When the railroad came through in 1854 the place became Rapid Ann Station, after the customary name of the river. In 1886 it settled on Rapidan.

moments.title: Waddell Memorial Presbyterian Church
moments.text: A Carpenter Gothic church of 1874 in board-and-batten siding, with a rose window in the middle stage of its tower and a belfry above.

moments.title: Rapidan Passenger Depot
moments.text: The depot sits at the junction where Route 615 ends, on a railroad whose Rapidan River bridge Confederate cavalry burned in April 1863.
